response:
**Service Name:** MindWell Sleep Study

**Overview:** The MindWell Sleep Study involves wearing a wrist sensor for 8 weeks while using a sleep-tracking app. The study aims to understand its effects on insomnia.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Participation**: You're asked to wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks, and complete weekly surveys. This is the main activity you'll be doing as a participant.
* **Risks**: There's a low risk of skin irritation from the sensor strap. If you experience this, it's not clear what you should do or who to contact for help.
* **Data Sharing**: Your personal data (information that can directly identify you) won't be shared with anyone outside the research team. However, **de-identified data (data that has been made unrecognizable, or "blind," to prevent identification)** may be shared with other universities. This means data that could be linked to you might be shared with other researchers.
* **Withdrawal**: You can stop participating at any time without penalty or consequence.
* **Compensation**: Upon completing the study, you'll receive $75 as a gesture of appreciation.

**Concerns:** The Terms of Service don't clearly outline what happens if you experience any issues with the wrist sensor, such as skin irritation or difficulties with using the app. There's no dedicated support process or clear contact for reporting technical problems or health concerns. 

The Terms of Service say that data, de-identified or not, may be shared with collaborators. This means the data, including sensitive information about you, will be shared without your direct consent.

You can contact the Institutional Review Board (IRB) at irb@example.edu if you have questions about this study.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

- Risk is minimal; mainly possible skin irritation.

- Withdrawal is allowed at any time without penalty.
- Compensation is $75 on completion.

**Service Name:** Microsoft Services Agreement

The Microsoft Services Agreement governs the relationship between you (the user) and Microsoft. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** The Agreement applies to all products and services listed on Microsoft's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** If you submit content to Microsoft (e.g., photos, messages), the company can use it to operate, improve, or train its AI/ML systems. This will happen only if your settings allow it. Microsoft follows the applicable law when doing so.
* **Privacy:** The company crosses-references its published Privacy Policy, which explains how it collects and processes personal data. 
* **What You Can and Can't Do:** The Agreement doesn't specify any restrictions on the services you can use.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement for specific reasons.
 
A few things to note:

* **Auto-renewal:** Some trial offers may require automatic renewal, so be sure to understand the terms before signing up. If the offer renews, and you don't want to continue, you may face additional fees.
* **Data Export:** The updated Agreement adds a new section on "exportable data." We don't have enough information on how this applies (the previous version made no mention of it). If you're concerned about data export, we recommend verifying the details in the actual agreement.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The Agreement requires **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (you can't join a group lawsuit)**, but you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
 

Keep in mind that these terms and conditions are subject to change. To ask questions or get help, follow the contact information provided in the Agreement.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

response:
**Service Name:** Microsoft Services Agreement (Effective 2024)

**Summary:**
These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Microsoft when using their products and services. They outline key provisions like content usage, privacy, dispute resolution, and termination.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** Microsoft uses your submitted content (e.g., text, photos, videos) to operate, improve, and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems, depending on your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** Microsoft's published Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is collected and processed. The Terms of Service direct you to this policy for more information.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The default method for resolving disputes is through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, this applies to most updated terms, and you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions described in the live document.

**Clauses potentially harmful to users:**

* **Bind arbitration and class-action waivers:** Although users have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, this clause might limit your ability to sue Microsoft in court or join a class-action lawsuit if you don't opt-out.
* **Use of user-submitted content:** While the Terms of Service don't specify how user content will be used, stating it's used "to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems" might raise concerns about data exploitation.

**Other important notes:**

* **Moderation and enforcement:** Microsoft provides external policy pages for moderation and enforcement clarifications. These might be useful for understanding how the company handles user content and behavior.
* **Xbox data tracking:** Microsoft now addresses third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data on Xbox, and has updated family settings on third-party platforms for kids. These changes aim to provide more transparency and control for users.

Please review the Terms of Service, especially the mentioned clauses, to ensure you understand the implications of using Microsoft's products and services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (2023 → 2024) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]
- The updated terms take effect in 2024 and replace the 2023 version.
- Key change: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.

- Users should review the cross-referenced Privacy Policy to understand data handling.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to your relationship with OpenAI and the products and services they offer.

**Harmful Clauses to the User:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This means you must resolve disputes through private arbitration, rather than going to court. You can't join a class-action lawsuit, even if many others have similar complaints.
* ** Binding Arbitration:** This is a private dispute process instead of a public court process. While intended to be more efficient, it may not provide the same level of protections or rights as a traditional court.

**Notable Exceptions:**
- Users with accounts from Steam (Valve) can opt out of mandatory arbitration, as Steam removed this requirement in 2024.

Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions (described in the live document). For questions about these terms, refer to the company's published legal contact information.

Remember that you can review the full Terms of Service at the specified links.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

**Service Name:** OpenAI Services Agreement (Business/API)

**Key Provisions:**

* The OpenAI Services Agreement governs your relationship with OpenAI and applies to their various business services, including API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team, and more.
* You agree to provide OpenAI with content, which they use to improve and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* Personal data is handled as outlined in OpenAI's separate Privacy Policy.
* Any disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers.
* Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* Questions about the terms should be directed to OpenAI's published legal contact information.

**Provisions That May be Harmful to the User:**

* Class-action waivers mean you give up your right to join a group lawsuit if you have a similar complaint against OpenAI. This can make it harder to hold the company accountable in certain situations.
* The requirement for binding arbitration might limit your ability to take OpenAI to court if you feel they have wronged you.
* The terms of service may not provide clear protections or remedies for users who experience harm or loss due to OpenAI's services.

Please note that this is a plain-language summary, and you should review the actual terms and conditions if you have specific concerns or questions about how they might affect you.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

- Key change: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs.
- The new terms govern OpenAI Services Agreement (business/API) for users of OpenAI.
- Users should review the cross-referenced Privacy Policy to understand data handling.
- The previous version of the terms is available for comparison at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/.

**Service Name:** The Terms of Service for Anthropic's Consumer Terms govern the relationship between you, the user, and Anthropic, a company that operates various AI-driven products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to products and services listed on Anthropic's official terms page. If a product or service is not on this list, it is not governed by these Terms.
* **Content and License:** You grant Anthropic permission to use your submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Anthropic's published Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The Terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions outlined in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions, visit Anthropic's published legal contact information.

**Potential Areas of Concern:**

* **Data Use:** Anthropic may use your submitted content to improve their AI/ML systems. While this is intended to improve the service, it's unclear how this affects your personal data.
* **Class-Action Waiver:** The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may limit your ability to participate in group lawsuits or join a class action against Anthropic.
* **Termination:** The Terms don't specify the conditions under which either party can terminate the agreement. This may leave you at risk of having your account terminated without notice or explanation.

The Terms of Service do not address issues like:

* What happens if Anthropic's AI/ML systems make errors or have unintended consequences?
* How long will Anthropic retain your content after termination?
* What are the consequences of violating Anthropic's Acceptable Use Policy?

These are concerns you'll need to discuss individually with a representative or review in more detail through their official contact channels.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.

**Service Name:** The Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service (API)

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Anthropic, a company that provides AI and machine learning (AI/ML) services. The key provisions are as follows:

* **Scope:** The terms apply to Anthropic's products and services, as described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant Anthropic permission to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Anthropic's published Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In the event of a dispute, you agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, you can opt out within 30 days of creating a new account. Note that some services, like Steam, are exempt from this rule.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions outlined in the live document.

**Key Points to Note:**

* **Data processing:** Anthropic will use your submitted content to train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. Be aware that your data may be processed in this way.
* **Dispute resolution:** The arbitration clause can limit your ability to pursue class-action lawsuits or take your dispute to court.
* **Limited termination rights:** While either party can terminate the agreement, the conditions for doing so are not explicitly stated in this summary.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding arbitration with class-action waivers:** This provision can limit your ability to pursue class-action lawsuits or take your dispute to court.
* **Limited termination rights:** The conditions for terminating the agreement are not explicitly stated, which may leave you with limited options if you need to exit the agreement.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** Facebook and Meta Terms of Service

These terms outline the rules and expectations for using Meta's products and services, including Facebook. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to all Meta products and services listed on the official terms page. Using any of these products means you agree to these terms.

**Content and License:** When you upload content to Meta's products, you grant Meta a license to use it for various purposes, such as improving and training AI and ML systems. The terms also mention that Meta will use your content only in accordance with your settings and applicable law.

**Privacy:** The terms don't explicitly state how Meta collects and processes your personal data. Instead, they reference Meta's published Privacy Policy, which explains these details.

**Dispute Resolution:** Most of these terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you can't band together with others to sue Meta even if many people share the same issue. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Termination:** Either you or Meta can terminate the agreement under certain circumstances, as described in the live document.

Some clauses that may be concerning to users:

* **Binding arbitration with class-action waivers:** This can make it harder to challenge Meta's policies and may limit the potential damages you can recover in case of a dispute.
* **Lack of explicit information on data collection and processing:** Reviewing Meta's Privacy Policy is essential to understand how your personal data is used.

Remember to review Meta's Privacy Policy and understand your settings to see how they affect your content and data usage. Additionally, be aware of the terms' provisions on dispute resolution and termination.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

**Service Name: Instagram Terms of Use**

These are the terms and conditions you agree to when using Instagram, a photo and video-sharing platform owned by Meta. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Relationship with Meta:** These terms outline your relationship with Meta and apply to your use of Instagram and its related services.

**Content and Licensing:** When you upload content to Instagram, you grant Meta (Instagram) a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute, and modify that content. This means they can use it to improve their AI systems, but you still control how your content is shared on your account, subject to applicable laws.

**Privacy:** The terms point to Meta's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed. You should review their Privacy Policy to understand what data Instagram collects and how they use it.

**Dispute Resolution:** To resolve disputes, binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is required, with some exceptions. However, you have a 30-day window to opt-out of arbitration when creating a new account.

**Termination:** Either you or Meta can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

Some provisions may be considered potentially harmful to users:

* **Grant of a non-exclusive license to Meta**: While Meta can use your content to improve their services, this clause might be seen as exploitative, as you may have contributed to the improvement of their business without direct compensation.
* **Requirement of binding arbitration**: This may limit your ability to seek redress in a court of law, potentially favoring Meta.
* **Lack of clarity on content usage**: While the terms mention that you're in control of how your content is shared on your account, it's uncertain how this interacts with Meta's non-exclusive license to modify and distribute your content.

Remember to review the full Terms of Service and Meta's published Privacy Policy to understand your rights and responsibilities more thoroughly.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

* Users should review and carefully consider their account settings to ensure they understand how their data will be shared.

Please note that the Terms of Service do not provide a detailed list of prohibited activities, but they do state that you must comply with all applicable laws and regulations.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

**Services Covered: TikTok US, as governed by these Terms of Service.**

These Terms of Service outline the rules and expectations between you and TikTok US when using TikTok. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

### Key Provisions:

1. **Scope:** These Terms apply to TikTok's products and services as mentioned on the company's official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** When you upload content to TikTok, you grant the company a license to use it, including for training and improving its AI and machine learning (ML) systems.
 * Note: TikTok will use your content "as is," with no guarantees or promises of quality.
3. **Privacy:** TikTok's published Privacy Policy outlines the data it collects and processes; this document only mentions that it cross-references the Privacy Policy.
4. **Dispute Resolution:** In the event of a dispute, both parties will engage in **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of going to court). There are class-action waivers, which means you can't join a group lawsuit. However, if you're a new user, you have a 30-day **opt-out window**, after which you'll be bound by these terms.
5. **Termination:** Either you or TikTok can terminate the Terms at any time, according to the conditions outlined in the agreement.
6. **Contact:** If you have questions about these Terms, you can reach out to TikTok through its published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses to Flag:**

* **Class-action waivers** can make it difficult for users to seek redress in the event of a group-wide issue.
* **Binding arbitration** removes your right to take a disagreement to court, potentially limiting your recourse in disputes.
* **Limited ability to opt-out** of arbitration, especially for new users, means you'll be committing to this process from the start.
* **"As is" usage of content** means TikTok makes no guarantees about the quality or safety of content used in its systems.

**Recommendation:**

While I've highlighted potential concerns, it's essential to review these Terms thoroughly and understand what you're agreeing to.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

Let's break down the key provisions:

1. **Scope**: These terms govern your interaction with Adobe and apply to the services you use.
2. **Content and License**: When you submit content, like images or text, to Adobe services, the company uses it to improve and operate its services, including AI and machine learning systems. However, Adobe claims it doesn't train generative AI models on customer cloud content, but this is specifically stated in the June 2024 update.
3. **Privacy**: Adobe's Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data it collects and how it's processed. These terms only reference this policy without providing additional details.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Adobe requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you may not join a class-action lawsuit against the company. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but don't rely on Steam (Valve) as they're an exception in the dataset.
5. **Termination**: Either Adobe or you can terminate the agreement under conditions outlined in the current document.
6. **Contact**: For questions or concerns, see Adobe's published legal contact information.

**Potential concerns for users:**

* **Data collection and use** (clause 3). Adobe may access your user content for various purposes, including improving AI and machine learning systems. Although it claims not to train generative AI models on customer cloud content, the phrasing may still be unclear to some users.
* **Class-action waiver** (clause 4). This means you can't join a class-action lawsuit against Adobe, even if you're affected by a large-scale issue.

These are the main points to understand about the Adobe General Terms of Use.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

**Service Name:** LinkedIn User Agreement

The LinkedIn User Agreement governs the user relationship with LinkedIn and applies to the products and services described on the company's official terms page. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms cover the relationship between you and LinkedIn, including all the products and services the company offers.
* **Content and License:** You grant LinkedIn permission to use your user-submitted content to improve and train AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means LinkedIn can use the content you post on the platform to make its services better.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which explains how LinkedIn collects and processes personal data. You can find this information at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most provisions in this agreement require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver (meaning you can't join a lawsuit with others who have similar claims). You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid this requirement.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Clauses that may be Harmful to the User:**

* **Class-action Waiver:** By agreeing to these terms, you give up your right to join a class-action lawsuit against LinkedIn. This means you'll deal with disputes individually, rather than as part of a group.
* **Binding Arbitration:** You'll need to resolve disputes through private arbitration instead of going to court. While this can be more efficient, it may limit your options and rights.

**Additional Notes:**

* LinkedIn can use your data to train AI/ML systems with your opt-out toggle in Settings.
* The 30-day opt-out window for new accounts allows you to avoid mandatory arbitration and class-action waivers.
* The company's Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.

Remember to review the company's published Privacy Policy to understand how your personal data is handled.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.

**Service Name:** GitHub Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with GitHub, the online platform for developers to share and collaborate on code. They cover how GitHub uses your data, how you interact with the service, and how disputes are resolved.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These Terms apply to the products and services offered by GitHub, as listed on their official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** When you share content on GitHub, they can use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means they can use the information you share on GitHub to improve their own services.
3. **Privacy:** The Terms reference GitHub's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed. However, the exact details on how your data is used are contained within the separate Privacy Policy.
4. **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute, you'll be required to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you can't join a lawsuit with others who have similar disputes.
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses to Consider:**

* **Data Sharing:** GitHub can share your personal data with their affiliates, including Microsoft, for AI/ML model development and training. You can opt out, but this won't prevent your data from being shared with existing affiliates at the time.
* **Arbitration:** The requirement for binding arbitration means you'll need to resolve disputes through a private process, rather than going to court. This can be a drawback for users seeking a more formal resolution process.
* **Class-action waivers:** With binding arbitration, you may not be able to join a lawsuit with others who have similar disputes. This can be a barrier to collective action and seeking justice on a larger scale.

Please review the details carefully before using GitHub's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

**Netflix Terms of Use Summary**

The Terms of Service apply to your relationship with Netflix, covering the products and services described on Netflix's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **What You Share:** When you share your Netflix account with others, called "extra members," you'll need to upgrade your subscription to a paid plan that includes additional members.
* **Content Usage:** Netflix uses your submitted content, such as feedback and suggestions, to improve its services. This may involve training its AI and machine learning systems.
* **Privacy:** The company's separate **Privacy Policy** explains what personal data it collects and how it's processed.
* **Disputes:** If a problem arises, you'll typically need to use **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**. This means you can't join a class-action lawsuit. However, if you're a new account holder, you have a 30-day window to opt out of this requirement.
* **Termination:** Either you or Netflix can end your subscription agreement under specified conditions.

**Potentially Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** This might disadvantage users, as they won't have the right to join a class-action lawsuit and may face costs associated with private arbitration.
* **Termination:** The agreement doesn't clearly specify the conditions under which Netflix may terminate the account, so this could potentially be used against users.

**Additional Information:**

* Questions about these terms can be directed to Netflix's published legal contact information at help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse.
* The updated Terms of Service supersede the 2023 version.

Please note that these terms are subject to change, and new provisions may be added in future updates. It's always a good idea to read through the terms carefully before using Netflix's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

**Service Overview**: The PayPal User Agreement explains the rules and guidelines that govern your relationship with PayPal when using their products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to various PayPal products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to PayPal, they use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The terms refer to PayPal's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: You may be required to resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.

**Potential Red Flags:**

* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement to use binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your options for seeking compensation or justice in case of a dispute.
* **Termination**: These terms allow PayPal to terminate the agreement without providing specific reasons or procedures for doing so, which could leave you without access to your account or funds.

**Additional Resources:**

* For questions about these terms, refer to PayPal's published legal contact information.
* PayPal publishes policy updates and diffs on their website for you to review.

It's essential to read and understand these terms, especially if you're concerned about the dispute resolution process or termination conditions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

service_name: Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions
response:
The Terms of Service govern the relationship between you and Apple regarding the company's media services, which includes features like iCloud, Apple Music, and the App Store. 

Here are the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services listed on Apple's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Apple (like photos or music), the company can use it to improve its artificial intelligence systems, but only according to your settings and relevant laws.
* **Privacy**: Apple's published Privacy Policy explains how it collects and processes personal data. You can read this policy separately.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You may have to settle disputes with Apple through private arbitration (a process where a neutral third party makes a decision instead of going to court). This includes a class-action waiver (which means you can't be part of a group lawsuit).
* **Termination**: Either you or Apple can end this agreement, but you should check the live document for specific conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions or concerns, you can find Apple's contact information on its website.

Some provisions may be concerning:

* **Arbitration**: The Terms of Service require private arbitration for disputes, which can limit your ability to seek redress in a public court. Additionally, the class-action waiver means you can't join a class-action lawsuit.
* **Data use**: Apple's ability to use your submitted content for its AI systems might be concerning, especially if you're not receiving clear benefits in exchange. It's essential to review the Privacy Policy to understand how your data is processed.

Please review these Terms carefully, and consider seeking external advice if you have concerns.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

**iCloud Terms and Conditions**

These terms govern your relationship with Apple and cover the products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services listed on Apple's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Apple uses user-submitted content for their operations, improvement, and training of AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The company cross-references their published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers. However, new accounts have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but the conditions are described in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **End-to-end encryption:** Apple has implemented Advanced Data Protection, which provides end-to-end encryption. However, this may lead to issues if you forget your password or lose access to your account.
* **Arbitration clause:** The binding arbitration with class-action waivers may disadvantage users in the event of a dispute.

**Other Notes:**

* Apple collects user-submitted content and uses it to improve their operations and train AI/ML systems.
* The company has cross-referenced their published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of personal data collected.

**Contact:**

For questions about these terms, please refer to Apple's published legal contact information at https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

Let's break down the key provisions of the Pinterest Terms of Service.

**Service Name:** These Terms of Service apply to "products and services described on the company's official terms page". For most people, this means the Pinterest website and mobile app.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content on Pinterest, you're allowing the company to use it to operate its services, improve them, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms of Service don't explain how your personal data is collected or processed, but they cross-reference Pinterest's separate **Privacy Policy**, which you should check for more information.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's a dispute, most accounts will have to go through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with class-action waivers, although you can opt out within 30 days of creating your account.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement if they follow the conditions described in the live document.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* The **Dispute Resolution** clause might be a concern for some users. Binding arbitration and class-action waivers can limit users' ability to seek justice in a public court setting. This can make it harder to hold companies accountable for wrongdoing.
* The **Termination** clause allows either party to end the agreement, but the terms don't specify the circumstances under which this might happen. Users should be cautious when posting content that might be considered sensitive or inflammatory.

**Important Notes:**

* Pinterest collects and uses **personal data** to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, but the Terms of Service don't explain how this data is handled.
* Users should review the **Privacy Policy** to understand how their personal data is collected and processed.
* The **Dispute Resolution** clause is a complex topic, and users should carefully review their rights and obligations before agreeing to the Terms of Service.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

**Service Name:** Tumblr Terms of Service

The Tumblr Terms of Service outline the rules and guidelines that Tumblr users must follow when using the service. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services provided by Tumblr, as listed on their official terms page.

**Content and License:** When you post content on Tumblr, you're granting them a license to use it for their own purposes, including training their AI/ML systems. However, the company will respect your settings and applicable law. You can opt-out of sharing your content with third-party AI partners in your account settings.

**Privacy:** Tumblr uses your personal data as described in their published Privacy Policy. The terms don't go into detailed specifics about data collection and processing.

**Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Tumblr, you'll have to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window if you create a new account.

**Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, and the terms describe the conditions for doing so.

Now, let's flag some potentially problematic clauses.

* **Use of public content for AI training:** When you post public content on Tumblr, you should be aware that the company might share it with its AI partners for training purposes. While you can opt-out of third-party sharing, there's no guarantee that your content won't be used for AI development elsewhere.
* **Binding arbitration:** By using Tumblr, you might waive your right to access a court. While arbitration can be a faster and more private process, it may not provide the same level of justice as a court trial.
* **Termination on notice:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but the terms don't provide clear guidelines on what that means in practice. You should be aware that Tumblr might suspend or close your account at any time.

Overall, while the updated terms seem to address the sharing of public content for AI training, there are still some concerns around the use of personal data and dispute resolution.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** Dropbox Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all products and services offered by Dropbox, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Dropbox uses your content to improve and operate its services, AI, and Machine Learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and the law.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is collected and processed as outlined in Dropbox's published Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users **must** go to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) if a dispute arises, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions listed in the document.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, refer to Dropbox's published contact information.

**Clauses that May Be Harmful to the User:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers**: As mentioned in the Dispute Resolution section, most users are required to go to binding arbitration, making it difficult to join class-action lawsuits. This can limit users' ability to seek justice if many people have been affected in a similar way.
* **No Opt-Out for Existing Users**: There is no mention of allowing existing users to opt-out of mandatory arbitration.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Key Provisions:**

* These Terms of Service govern your relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
* 23andMe collects and uses your personal data to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, as per your settings and applicable law.
* The company cross-references its published Privacy Policy for information on the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
* In case of a dispute, you're required to use binding arbitration instead of going to court, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* The company can terminate the agreement under certain conditions, and you can also terminate it with or without cause.

**Harmful Clauses for the User:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** If you don't opt out within 30 days, any disputes related to a data breach (like the one in October 2023) will be resolved through binding arbitration instead of court. This can limit your ability to seek compensation or join a class-action lawsuit.
* **Class-Action Limitations:** The terms also limit your ability to participate in class-action lawsuits related to disputes with 23andMe.
* **Shortened Dispute Notice Window:** If you have a dispute, you'll need to provide a notice earlier than under previous versions.

**Please note that these Terms of Service are subject to change, and you're advised to review them regularly for updates.**
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Service Name:** Roblox Terms of Use (as of 2024).

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms govern your relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services listed on Roblox's official terms page.
* **Default Private Accounts for Minors**: If you're under 13, your Roblox account is private by default. You'll need a parent's consent to share your information with others.
* **Content and Usage**: Roblox can use the content you submit, subject to your settings and applicable laws, to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy**: The Terms cross-reference Roblox's Privacy Policy, which describes the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users must go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, but you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, following the conditions described in the document.
* **Contact**: Questions about the Terms can be directed to Roblox's published legal contact information.

**Clauses That May Be Harmful to the User:**

* The requirement of binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, which may limit users' ability to seek redress in a public court.
* The clause allowing Roblox to use user-submitted content for its own purposes, which may raise concerns about data ownership or exploitation.

**Other Points to Note:**

* The Terms can be updated or changed by Roblox at any time.
* You should regularly check the Terms and Roblox's Privacy Policy for updates.
* You're responsible for complying with applicable laws and regulations when using Roblox's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .
